label: Aristotle, Metaphysics IV.7, 1012a5-9: It is absurd that there is an intermediate beside every…
interpretation: 'There must be an intermediate beside all contradictions, unless one is speaking for the sake of argument; so that one will neither speak truly nor not speak truly, and there will be something beside being and not-being, so that there will also be a change beside generation and destruction.' A reductio of the universal intermediate thesis, applied to the contradictions 'speaks truly / does not' and 'is / is not'. Formally it is a corollary of LOGIC-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE-NOT-DENIABLE (no instance can be denied, so not every one), and like that result it refutes positing intermediates, not withholding assent. Not separately formalized.
